probes.description: Three series: the sample number, a wave between 0 and 100, and a rate that follows it.
probes.label: Synthetic metrics

probes.description: A snapshot table whose rows move on by one id per sample, so rows leave at the top and arrive at the bottom.
probes.label: Synthetic rows

probes.description: The phase (even or odd) and the sample count.
probes.label: Synthetic status

probes.description: Two snapshot tables from one sample. Items move on by one id per sample, as the table probe's rows do, in five groups, with group facets and departed rows; the even view keeps the items with an even id. Groups count the items of each group, built from the source's own state rather than read from SQL Server.
probes.label: Synthetic grid

probes.description: An append table that grows by logRows messages a sample (levels 0 to 3). With lateEvery, one message of every n-th sample becomes visible a sample late, after higher ids, as a slow writer's commit would. A filter or a new logLevel (the lowest level shown) starts the table again under the new predicate, and start picks its first row.
probes.label: Synthetic log

probes.description: A snapshot of rows rows of 23 columns, the shape of a session list, for the snapshot churn benchmark. Its status reports how many gen2 collections the backend has run.
probes.label: Synthetic wide rows

probes.description: The server at a glance, in one DMV query: SQL Server's CPU (its schedulers' non-preemptive time), runnable tasks, batch requests, compilations and re-compilations per second, and user sessions. Rates use the server's own clock (ms_ticks), and a restart starts them again.
probes.label: Overview

probes.description: The databases that are not plainly online and open to everyone, from sys.databases: their state (sys.databases.state), user access (0 multi, 1 single, 2 restricted), read-only and standby flags. Needs no server permission; a login sees the databases sys.databases shows it.
probes.label: Database states

probes.description: How far each running RESTORE DATABASE or RESTORE LOG, and each database recovery (DB STARTUP), has come (sys.dm_exec_requests.percent_complete, whole percent). A restore runs in its session's database, so the database it restores is the one its request holds an exclusive database lock on (sys.dm_tran_locks, read only for those requests).
probes.label: Restore and recovery progress

probes.description: How many SQL Server Agent jobs are running: msdb.dbo.sysjobactivity rows of the Agent's current session (the newest in msdb.dbo.syssessions) that started and have not stopped, as Job Activity Monitor counts them. A login msdb refuses gets PERMISSION_DENIED as a value.
probes.label: Running Agent jobs

probes.description: Each availability group's synchronization health (0 not healthy, 1 partially healthy, 2 healthy) and this replica's role (0 resolving, 1 primary, 2 secondary), from sys.dm_hadr_availability_group_states and sys.dm_hadr_availability_replica_states. A server without Always On has no rows.
probes.label: Availability group health

sources.description: Generated values for protocol, renderer and smoke tests. It runs no SQL, so any connection id is accepted; a disconnect of that id still ends it.
sources.label: Synthetic

sources.description: SQL Server's own activity, read from server DMVs on the connection's " - Activity Monitor" pool (READ UNCOMMITTED, LOCK_TIMEOUT 1000, DEADLOCK_PRIORITY LOW).
sources.label: Activity Monitor

sources.description: The states Object Explorer shows as chips on its nodes (docs/object-explorer.md, Live status): one view per connected server while Object Explorer shows, on the server pool (" - Activity Monitor": READ UNCOMMITTED, LOCK_TIMEOUT 1000, DEADLOCK_PRIORITY LOW). It never reloads the tree.
sources.label: Object Explorer status
